27: 1. A beis din is never fewer than three, etc. — The Sma wrote that this is rabbinic, but by Torah law one judge suffices, and so the Rambam writes explicitly in perek 2 of Hilchos Sanhedrin, that he paskens like Rav Acha, and so it is implied in the Asheri (Rosh) at the start of the first perek of Sanhedrin, and not like what is written in the Ir Shushan — see there, end of his words. But in my humble opinion the words of the Ir Shushan are correct. For we say in the Gemara, first perek of Sanhedrin: what is the difference between Rava and Rav Acha? For Rava does not hold like Shmuel that two who judged, their ruling is a valid ruling, while Rav Acha does hold like Shmuel. And since we have established that the halacha is not like Shmuel — as below at the start of se'if 2 — then perforce we hold like Rava, that by Torah law we require three mumchim, since the verse "elohim" is written three times; only that Chazal enacted that three hedyotos suffice, so as not to lock the door before borrowers. And the view of the Rosh too is proven to be this way, according to what I wrote, for he paskened like Rabbi Abahu and not like Shmuel. And what he wrote at the beginning of the perek — the words of Rav Acha too are only to teach that we require one who is gamir, and to teach that on this point Rava does not argue with Rav Acha; for if he did argue, the Gemara should have said "this is the difference between them." So it appears to me in the view of the Rosh, and not like the Sma and the Bach in his view. And the Rosh wrote further, explicitly, that the halacha is like Rabbi Abahu, since we hold that from Abaye and Rava onward the halacha is like the later authorities, and we say in the Gemara that Rava does not hold like Shmuel — end of his words — and the Beis Yosef brings it. And from here too there is a great difficulty on the Sma and the Bach in the view of the Rosh. And this is precise in the view of the Ir Shushan, for below in se'if 2 he wrote: since from the verses we derive that there must be three, from the three "elohim," therefore fewer than three, their ruling is not a valid ruling, etc. — and this is exactly according to the sugya of the Gemara that I mentioned.

2. And further, on the Rambam it is difficult for me: since he paskened that fewer than three, their ruling is not a valid ruling, how did he write in accordance with the words of Rav Acha? For we say in the Gemara that according to Rav Acha the law of Shmuel holds. And likewise it is difficult for me on the Sma"g. And further it is difficult for me on their words: for in the Gemara, perek HaChovel (Bava Kamma daf 84) and perek HaMegaresh (Gittin daf 88 amud beis), it states explicitly that the reason we judge admissions and loans [nowadays] is because we act as agents of them, of the "elohim"; and so the Rambam himself writes in perek 3 of Hilchos Sanhedrin, and the Sma"g, in this language: "therefore we judge admissions and loans and the like outside the land, even though the beis din of chutz la'aretz are not 'elohim,' for they perform the agency of the beis din of Eretz Yisrael," end quote. This shows that by Torah law we do not judge admissions and loans except through mumchim, and that is like Rava, for according to Rav Acha, by Torah law a single hedyot suffices, as is proven explicitly in the Gemara, and so it is in the Asheri (Rosh). And perhaps one can resolve the words of the Rambam and the Sma"g with difficulty, but the main point appears that we hold like Rava and not like Shmuel, and as is implied in perek HaChovel and perek HaMegaresh, that we require "elohim." And so too the view of the Rif appears explicitly, for he did not bring the words of Rav Acha at all, and wrote the beginning of the sugya in the first perek of Sanhedrin in accordance with Rava, that by Torah law we require three mumchim — see there. And so wrote the Ravan, daf 111, start of amud gimmel, that the sugya is like Rava, that we require three mumchim, and on account of locking the door before borrowers three hedyotos suffice, etc. And so wrote the Nimukei Yosef explicitly. At the time I wrote the above words I did not have before me the sefer Kesef Mishneh, for I learned this while fleeing from the wars of the destroyers, and now I have looked into the Kesef Mishneh and seen that he sensed there the difficulty I raised above on the Rambam — how did he pasken like Rav Acha and yet immediately write that two who judged, their ruling is not a valid ruling — and he brings there the responsum of the Rashba, who resolves the Rambam's words on this, and so too in the sefer Lechem Mishneh. And in my humble opinion their words are forced in this, and also the language of "what is between them" and "the difference between them is, etc." in the Gemara does not imply so — analyze this. And in any case the rest of the difficulties I wrote above on the Rambam remain, and the Rashba and the Kesef Mishneh and the Lechem Mishneh did not sense them — see there.
